record.paper_title: Open problems on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundary
record.original_question: Let C be a simple closed planar curve in ℝ³, and let Σ be a compact embedded surface of constant mean curvature with boundary C. What hypotheses on the boundary curve C guarantee that Σ lies entirely on one side of the plane containing C? In particular, what can be proved when C is convex?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.2. Under what conditions on the boundary, a compact embedded cmc surface of ℝ³ spanning a planar closed curve C is contained in one side of the boundary plane? and if C is convex?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a simple closed curve contained in a plane $\Pi \subset \mathbb{R}^3$, and let $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a compact embedded smooth surface with constant mean curvature whose boundary $\partial\Sigma = C$. 

(a) Find geometric or analytic hypotheses on the planar Jordan curve $C$ which guarantee that $\Sigma$ is contained in one of the two closed half-spaces determined by the plane $\Pi$.

(b) In particular, prove or disprove the following: if $C$ is a convex planar curve, then every such compact embedded constant mean curvature surface $\Sigma$ with $\partial\Sigma = C$ lies entirely on one side of the plane $\Pi$.
artifact.category_tag: constant mean curvature surfaces with boundary
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of identifying conditions on a planar Jordan boundary curve $C$ that force a compact embedded CMC surface spanning $C$ to lie on one side of the boundary plane appears to remain open in general. Classical results show that if one assumes a priori that $\Sigma$ lies on one side of $\Pi$ and $C$ is a circle, then $\Sigma$ must be a spherical cap. Recent partial progress (e.g., assuming local convexity of $\Sigma$, or strict convexity of $C$ together with extra hypotheses) yields the spherical-cap conclusion, but the general convex-boundary case is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: An extension of Liebmann's Theorem to hypersurfaces with boundary
status_evidence.snippet: A locally convex, embedded, compact, connected CMC hypersurface bounded by a closed strictly convex planar curve is a spherical cap.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress under additional convexity assumptions; general case not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Surfaces with constant mean curvature in Euclidean space (Camino survey)
status_evidence.snippet: The structure of compact CMC surfaces bounded by a given Jordan curve is far from being understood.
status_evidence.claim: The general one-sidedness/classification problem for CMC surfaces with planar boundary remains open.

status_evidence.title: CMC surfaces in a half-space of R^3 with boundary in the boundary of the half-space
status_evidence.snippet: Studies CMC surfaces bounded by convex planar curves under the a priori assumption of being in a half-space.
status_evidence.claim: Strong results are known under the one-sided assumption, but the assumption itself is what one wants to derive.
